items.title: Sudan: Nobody Hands Over a Gun for Nothing
items.description: [African Arguments] On 6 October, Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan said again that there would be no negotiations with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, or 'any other party', and that the war would go on until victory. A day earlier, Donald Trump's envoy Massad Boulos had disclosed a meeting with him in Egypt. Washington is pushing a 90-day humanitarian truce and, according to sources cited by Reuters, made Burhan's visa for the UN General Assembly conditional on it.
items.titleIt: Sudan: Nobody Hands Over a Gun for Nothing

items.title: Opinion: The Horn of Africa Deserves Peace Not Crisis and Instability
items.description: Yet, behind these crises are millions of people who share deep historical, cultural, economic, and social ties. items.title: Sudan: WFP Strongly Condemns Attack On Trucks In South Kordofan, Killing One Driver
items.description: One driver was killed in the air strike. We extend our deepest condolences to his family, friends and colleagues. The contracted trucks were en route from Dilling to Kadugli and clearly marked as humanitarian vehicles. Additional details regarding the circumstances of the incident, including the extent of the damage to the food cargo, are still being collected. WFP calls for a prompt and impartial investigation into this incident and for those responsible for any violations to be held accountable.
